checks.label: Fingerprint Enrolled
checks.description: Check if fingerprint authentication is enrolled
checks.remediation: Enroll a fingerprint in Settings > Security > Fingerprint for stronger auth.

checks.label: Face Unlock Status
checks.description: Face unlock may be less secure than fingerprint
checks.remediation: Disable face unlock in Settings > Security and use fingerprint or PIN instead.

checks.label: Auto-Lock After Biometric
checks.remediation: Set a short auto-lock timeout in Settings > Security > Screen lock timeout.

checks.label: Biometric Keyguard Enabled
checks.description: Biometric keyguard should be enabled for secure unlock
checks.remediation: Enable biometric keyguard in Settings > Security > Biometrics.

checks.label: Biometric Strength
checks.description: Biometric auth should be 'STRONG' (not 'WEAK'). Empty if no biometric hardware.
checks.remediation: Use a device with STRONG biometric hardware or fall back to PIN/password.

checks.label: Biometric Template Storage Permissions
checks.command: P=''; for d in /data/system/users/0/fpdata /data/vendor_de/0/fpdata /data/vendor_de/0/facedata /data/system/users/0/facedata; do [ -e "$d" ] && P="$P $(ls -ld $d 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1" "$3":"$4" "$NF}')"; done; [ -z "$P" ] && echo NO_TEMPLATE_DIR_VISIBLE || echo "$P"
checks.description: Reports the ownership and permissions of the directories holding fingerprint and face templates. Templates must never be readable outside the biometric HAL and the secure environment, and on a correctly built device the directory is either absent from the Linux view entirely, because the template lives in the TEE, or is restricted to the biometric UID. NO_TEMPLATE_DIR_VISIBLE is the strongest outcome and is treated as passing. Reported for review because the path and owner are OEM-specific and a visible directory with tight permissions is also acceptable.
checks.remediation: Confirm templates are stored in the TEE or in a directory readable only by the biometric HAL UID, and that they are wiped on user removal and factory reset.

checks.label: Authentication Lockout and Gatekeeper State
checks.command: L=$(dumpsys lock_settings 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'lockout|failed|throttl|strong.?auth' | head -8); G=$(ls -l /data/system/gatekeeper.*.key /data/system/locksettings.db 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1" "$NF}' | tr '\n' ' '); [ -z "$L" ] && [ -z "$G" ] && echo NO_LOCK_SETTINGS_VISIBLE || echo "${L:-no_dump} | files=${G:-none}"
checks.description: Reports lockout, failed-attempt and strong-auth state from lock_settings, plus the permissions on the Gatekeeper key blobs and the lock settings database. Gatekeeper enforces escalating delays after failed unlock attempts, and its counter must live in tamper-resistant storage (see ATT-026 on RPMB) or the throttling can be reset by rolling back the counter, turning a four-digit PIN into an offline brute force. Reported for review because the dump format is OEM-specific and a restricted or absent view is itself a good sign.
checks.remediation: Confirm the Gatekeeper failure counter is backed by RPMB or equivalent replay-protected storage rather than plain userdata, and that the key blobs are not readable outside the system UID.
